liner.body_md:
## What listeners single out

- **My Brother Esau** (3 reviews): Played more playfully than usual, though the band seemed to be losing confidence in the song; Reviewer calls it a nice version [26][31][34]
- **Hell In A Bucket** (2 reviews): Healy used the echo chamber to bounce Weir's vocals around the arena, with motorcycle sound effects revving; Reviewer considers it very good [24][32]
- **Funiculi Funicula** (1 review): Show opened with this tune and a goofy Addams Family tuning, after two strong nights in a row [26]
- **Jack Straw** (1 review): Reviewer hears a solid but not spirited version, measured against the 10/18/83 standard; the Funiculi intro precedes it [31]
- **Far From Me** (1 review): Brent delivers a heartfelt, strong version [34]
- **Iko Iko** (1 review): Garcia played it hard and tacked several extra choruses onto the end [24]
- **Looks Like Rain** (1 review): Garcia bent a note about three and a half minutes in that sustained roughly six seconds [24]
- **He's Gone** (1 review): Reviewer disliked that it produced no jam after Looks Like Rain [28]

## Setlist highlights

- **Addams Family Tuning**: rare: 5 archived performances [36]

## The recordings

- **gd1987-09-20.137407.sbd.miller.flac24** (recommended): soundboard; 22 songs; 154 min [1]
- **gd87-09-20.sbd.eD.16128.sbeok.shnf**: soundboard; 22 songs; 146 min; rated 3.73/5 by 10 [4]. Said about its sound: Reviewer describes the soundboard sound as good [32]
- **gd87-09-20.schoeps.willy.15410.sbeok.shnf**: audience recording; 20 songs; 152 min; rated 2/5 by 1 [12]. Said about its sound: Audience recording sounds okay but with a bit too much crowd; reviewer found the Garden's acoustics exceptionally clear [27]
- **gd1987-09-20.nak300.damico.90492.sbeok.flac16**: source not stated; 21 songs; 149 min; rated 5/5 by 2 [17]. Said about its sound: Recording has superb presence, as if you were in the room [33]

## Around the show

- Reviewer's third show; it closed a five-show 1987 Madison Square Garden run that helped win over midtown locals and sports fans [25]
- Reviewer guesses the band was ready to leave town after four earlier Garden shows [28]
- Audience is attentive and sings along at exactly the right moments on this recording [33]
- Reviewer's friends attended this run's last three shows and dismissed this one at the time [34]
- Reviewer calls it inconsistent: opening songs of each set are hot, rest below average for the 1980s [28]
- Reviewer ranks it among the best of 1987, alongside the Hartford show [30]
- Reviewer rates it second-worst of the Garden run but still very good, with a first set lacking cowboy tunes [32]

## Tapers and lineage

- **gd1987-09-20.137407.sbd.miller.flac24**: transferred by Charlie Miller; source: SBD > Cassette Master (TDK SA-X90) [1]. Also: Two sets of masters were combined to complete the show, with pitch correction help from Joe B. Jones [1]
- **gd87-09-20.sbd.eD.16128.sbeok.shnf**: source: Master PCM>?>DAT>SONIC SOLUTIONS>CD>CD > EAC[secure] > SHN [4]
- **gd87-09-20.schoeps.willy.15410.sbeok.shnf**: source: AUD (Schoeps CMC 34's)>MC*>DAT>CD [12]
- **gd1987-09-20.nak300.damico.90492.sbeok.flac16**: taped by Joe D'Amico; transferred by Joe D'Amico; source: nak 300 mics w/ cp4 shotguns > sony d-5 D [17]

## Art and photos

- Poster by Robbi Cohn: [1987-09-18 Madison Square Garden, New York, NY, USA - Jerry Garcia](https://jerrygarcia.com/show/1987-09-18-madison-square-garden-new-york-ny-usa/) [37]

Garcia bent a note about three and a half minutes in that sustained roughly six seconds
Reviewer's third show; it closed a five-show 1987 Madison Square Garden run that helped win over midtown locals and sports fans
Reviewer cherished its pathos as the closer at the end of the long run
Show opened with this tune and a goofy Addams Family tuning, after two strong nights in a row
Played more playfully than usual, though the band seemed to be losing confidence in the song
Audience recording sounds okay but with a bit too much crowd; reviewer found the Garden's acoustics exceptionally clear
Reviewer found it lukewarm
Reviewer calls it inconsistent: opening songs of each set are hot, rest below average for the 1980s
Reviewer disliked that it produced no jam after Looks Like Rain
Reviewer guesses the band was ready to leave town after four earlier Garden shows
Reviewer ranks it among the best of 1987, alongside the Hartford show
Reviewer hears a solid but not spirited version, measured against the 10/18/83 standard; the Funiculi intro precedes it
Reviewer calls it a nice version
Reviewer rates it second-worst of the Garden run but still very good, with a first set lacking cowboy tunes
Reviewer considers it very good
Reviewer describes the soundboard sound as good
Audience is attentive and sings along at exactly the right moments on this recording
Recording has superb presence, as if you were in the room
Reviewer's friends attended this run's last three shows and dismissed this one at the time
Weir plays a late-era version before the song was shelved; good but a little rusty in places
Brent delivers a heartfelt, strong version
Two sets of masters were combined to complete the show, with pitch correction help from Joe B. Jones
Master PCM to DAT, then Sonic Solutions, CD, EAC secure extraction, and SHN, with resliced tracks
